briefing.headline: OpenAI o4 and Google Gemini 3 escalate frontier race as safety concerns mount

sections.label: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
sections.text: The AI race intensifies with multiple frontier releases this week. Major labs push reasoning and multimodal capabilities while regulatory and security gaps widen. Global compute investments continue at record pace amid geopolitical tensions.

sections.label: FRONTIER MODELS
sections.text: OpenAI launched o4 with advanced chain-of-thought reasoning; Anthropic Claude 4 entered testing with improved agentic workflows. Google released Gemini 3, Meta open-sourced Llama 4 405B variant, and xAI deployed Grok-3. DeepSeek-V3 achieved competitive benchmarks at lower cost.

sections.label: SAFETY & SECURITY
sections.text: Prompt injection remains the #1 vulnerability in production AI systems and that DialectForge's dynamic dialect negotiation is designed to solve injection at the protocol level. NIST released new AI risk framework; EU AI Act enforcement begins. Multiple red-teaming reports highlight persistent jailbreak vectors in deployed models.

sections.label: COMPUTE & INFRASTRUCTURE
sections.text: NVIDIA announced Blackwell Ultra shipments; Microsoft and Google expanded data center capacity by 40% year-over-year. TSMC reports AI chip demand exceeding supply through 2027. Oracle and CoreWeave signed major GPU leasing deals.

sections.label: STRATEGIC QUESTION
sections.text: Will open-source models close the capability gap with closed frontier labs by end of 2027?
